title: Akshay Kumar and Priyadarshan Are Reuniting for a Ninth Time. The Title Alone Will Give You Goosebumps.
excerpt: Their new comedy thriller is called Wicked Sunny — a direct callback to the iconic Mujhse Shaadi Karogi theme that still lives rent-free in every desi head.
body:
There are partnerships in Bollywood, and then there is **Akshay Kumar** and **Priyadarshan**. The actor-director duo that gave us *Hera Pheri*, *Bhool Bhulaiyaa*, and *Garam Masala* — essentially the holy trinity of Hindi comedy — are coming back together for film number nine. And the title? It's perfect.

The film is called ***Wicked Sunny***.

If that phrase just triggered a very specific instrumental theme in your head — the one that played every time Akshay's unhinged character Sunny showed up in *Mujhse Shaadi Karogi* (2004) — congratulations, you're a real one. That theme, goofy and menacing in equal measure, became one of Bollywood's most iconic background scores. Twenty-two years later, it's the name of an entire movie.

## A Comedy Thriller With an Edge

According to reports in *Bollywood Hungama*, **Wicked Sunny** will be a comedy thriller produced by **Ramesh Taurani** under the **Tips Films** banner. The screenplay has been written by Priyadarshan alongside **Rohan Shankar**, who also co-wrote the duo's recent blockbuster *Bhooth Bangla*.

> "The title does complete justice to the film's zone as well as its lead character. Wicked Sunny has strong recall value." — Source close to the production

What makes this particularly exciting is the promise that Akshay will appear in a "wacky comic avatar" that's distinctly different from his recent outings in *Bhooth Bangla* and *Welcome To The Jungle*. For a man who has been doing back-to-back comedies, the fact that the makers are positioning this as something tonally separate suggests they're swinging for the fences.

The film is expected to go on floors in **December 2026**.

## The Most Decorated Partnership in Hindi Comedy

Let's take a moment to appreciate what these two have built together. Here's the filmography:

- **Hera Pheri** (2000) — the undisputed GOAT of Hindi comedy
- **Garam Masala** (2005) — slapstick perfection
- **Bhagam Bhag** (2006) — chaotic and underrated
- **Bhool Bhulaiyaa** (2007) — horror-comedy before it was a genre
- **De Dana Dan** (2009) — maximalist madness
- **Khatta Meetha** (2010) — the last one before the long break
- **Bhooth Bangla** (2026) — the reunion that crossed ₹292 crore worldwide

Their eighth film, **Haiwaan**, co-starring **Saif Ali Khan**, hits theatres on **September 11, 2026**. So we're looking at three Akshay-Priyadarshan films either released or in the pipeline within the span of a single year. That's not a reunion — that's a full-blown renaissance.


## What This Means for Diaspora Audiences

For NRIs who grew up watching Akshay and Priyadarshan's comedies on pirated DVDs, at community hall screenings, and later on Netflix during the nostalgia era, this is a big deal. *Hera Pheri* and *Bhool Bhulaiyaa* aren't just films — they're cultural shorthand. Quote "Baburao" at any Indian gathering from New Jersey to Brampton and watch the room light up.

*Bhooth Bangla* proved the magic still works in theatres, earning nearly ₹200 crore domestically. If *Wicked Sunny* delivers on the promise of its title — bringing back that manic, anything-goes Akshay that made him the biggest comedy star in the country — the diaspora box office alone could be significant.

The fact that it's a comedy **thriller** also suggests a tighter structure than their purely farcical earlier work. Think *Bhool Bhulaiyaa* energy: funny, yes, but with actual stakes and a plot that keeps you guessing.

## The Bottom Line

Akshay Kumar turns 59 this September. Priyadarshan is 68. Neither of them is slowing down — and with *Wicked Sunny*, they seem to be deliberately reaching back to the exact energy that made them legends. The title alone is a statement of intent: this isn't a franchise sequel or a safe bet. It's an original, it's got swagger, and it knows exactly what you want from it.

The only question now is whether the film can live up to the theme song that inspired its name. If you need to refresh your memory, search "Wicked Sunny theme Mujhse Shaadi Karogi" on YouTube. You'll know within five seconds why this movie already has a fanbase.
